item.text: I’m reviewing the current structure again and picking the next refactor that improves the code’s shape without inventing unnecessary layers. The main candidate now is reducing duplication between heap building and heap validation inside the core heap class.

I’m moving result creation behind the core API instead of leaving it as demo knowledge. This makes `BuildHeapDemo` a true caller of the heap library rather than a second place that knows how to assemble heap state.

The next edit is in the heap engine itself. I’m centralizing “snapshot input, build heap copy, validate result” inside `IntArrayHeap` so that flow exists in one place instead of being spread between `BuildHeap` and `HeapBuildResult`.
I’m tightening the result type now so it becomes a passive value object instead of another place with orchestration logic. After this, creation will flow through `BuildHeap.analyze(...)` only.
I’m finishing the seam change in the demo now. It will stop constructing results directly and just consume the public heap API.
The refactor is in place. I’m compiling and running the same demo cases now to confirm the library boundary changed, but the observable behavior did not.
